explanation: Far from a black hole, its gravity is like that of any object with the same mass. If the Sun were swapped for a black hole of equal mass, Earth would keep its orbit.

claims.text: Black holes do not suck in everything around them; objects at a safe distance can orbit a black hole as they would any other body of the same mass.
At a distance, a black hole's gravity is the same as that of any other object with the same mass.
If the Sun were replaced by a black hole of the same mass, Earth's orbit would stay the same.
